46059-the-adopting-of-rosa-marie-a-seque.title: (_A Sequel to Dandelion Cottage_)
46059-the-adopting-of-rosa-marie-a-seque.creator: Unknown
46059-the-adopting-of-rosa-marie-a-seque.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It was not, however, the oldest, but four of the youngest citizens that rejoiced most in this unusual prolonging of summer; for the continued warm weather made it possible for those devoted friends, Jean Mapes, Marjory Vale, Mabel Bennett and little Bettie Tucker, to spend many a delightful hour in their precious Dandelion Cottage, the real, tumble-down house that was now, after so many narrow escapes, safely their very own.

arxiv-2109-07596.title: Direction-Assisted Beam Management in Full Duplex Millimeter Wave Massive MIMO Systems
arxiv-2109-07596.creator: Md Atiqul Islam 2 , George C. Alexandropoulos 4 , and Besma Smida 2
arxiv-2109-07596.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Md Atiqul Islam 2 , George C. Alexandropoulos 4 , and Besma Smida 2. Recent applications of the Full Duplex (FD) technology focus on enabling simultaneous control communication and data transmission to reduce the control information exchange overhead, which impacts end-to-end latency and spectral efficiency. In this paper, we present a simultaneous direction estimation and data transmission scheme for millimeter Wave (mmWave) massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, enabled by a recent FD MIMO technology with reduced hardware complexity Self-Interference (SI) cancellation.

arxiv-2112-11151.title: Efficient Classical Computation of Quantum Mean Values for Shallow QAOA Circuits
arxiv-2112-11151.creator: Wei-Feng Zhuang, Ya-Nan Pu, Hong-Ze Xu, Xudan Chai, Yanwu Gu, Yunheng Ma, Shahid Qamar, Chen Qian, Peng Qian, Xiao Xiao, Meng-Jun Hu, Dong E. Liu
arxiv-2112-11151.description: Abstract The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), which is a variational quantum algorithm, aims to give sub-optimal solutions of combinatorial optimization problems. It is widely believed that QAOA has the potential to demonstrate application-level quantum advantages in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum(NISQ) processors with shallow circuit depth.

arxiv-2212-06945.title: Variational Convexity of Functions in Banach Spaces
arxiv-2212-06945.creator: Pham Duy Khanh, Vu Vinh Huy Khoa, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Vo Thanh Phat
arxiv-2212-06945.description: Abstract Abstract . This paper addresses the study and characterizations of variational convexity of extended-real-valued functions on Banach spaces. This notion has been recently introduced by Rockafellar, and its importance has been already realized and applied to continuous optimization problems in finite-dimensional spaces.

arxiv-2309-10132.title: Ontology-Based Feedback to Improve Runtime Control for Multi-Agent Manufacturing Systems
arxiv-2309-10132.creator: Jonghan Lim, Leander Pfeiffer, Felix Ocker, Birgit Vogel-Heuser, Ilya Kovalenko
arxiv-2309-10132.description: Abstract Improving the overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) of machines on the shop floor is crucial to ensure the productivity and efficiency of manufacturing systems. To achieve the goal of increased OEE, there is a need to develop flexible runtime control strategies for the system. Decentralized strategies, such as multi-agent systems, have proven effective in improving system flexibility.

arxiv-2310-05662.title: On the lowest-frequency bandgap of 1D phononic crystals
arxiv-2310-05662.creator: J. González-Carbajal, M. Lemm and J. Garcia-Suarez
arxiv-2310-05662.description: Abstract . This manuscript puts forward and verifies an analytical approach to design phononic crystals that feature a bandgap at the lowest possible frequencies. This new approach is verified against numerical optimization. It rests on the exact form of the trace of the cumulative transfer matrix.

arxiv-2402-11922.title: Spatio-Temporal Few-Shot Learning via Diffusive Neural Network Generation
arxiv-2402-11922.creator: Yuan Yuan, Chenyang Shao, Jingtao Ding, Depeng Jin, Yong Li
arxiv-2402-11922.description: Abstract Spatio-temporal modeling is foundational for smart city applications, yet it is often hindered by data scarcity in many cities and regions. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel generative pre-training framework, GPD, for spatio-temporal few-shot learning with urban knowledge transfer.

arxiv-2405-17750.title: Magnitude-based Neuron Pruning for Backdoor Defense
arxiv-2405-17750.creator: Nan Li, Haoyu Jiang, Ping Yi
arxiv-2405-17750.description: Abstract Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are known to be vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing concerning threats to their reliable deployment. Recent research reveals that backdoors can be erased from infected DNNs by pruning a specific group of neurons, while how to effectively identify and remove these backdoor-associated neurons remains an open challenge.

arxiv-2410-03780.title: Reward-RAG: Enhancing RAG with Reward Driven Supervision
arxiv-2410-03780.creator: Thang Nguyen & Peter Chin & Yu-Wing Tai
arxiv-2410-03780.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce Reward-RAG, a novel approach designed to enhance the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model through Reward-Driven Supervision. Unlike previous RAG methodologies, which focus on training language models (LMs) to utilize external knowledge retrieved from external sources, our method adapts retrieval information to specific domains by employing CriticGPT to train a dedicated reward model.

arxiv-2509-25563.title: Inverse Optimal Feedback and Gain Margins for Unicycle Stabilization
arxiv-2509-25563.creator: Kwang Hak Kim, Velimir Todorovski, Miroslav Krstić
arxiv-2509-25563.description: Abstract The recent development of globally strict control Lyapunov functions (CLFs) for the challenging unicycle parking problem provides a foundation for pursuing optimality. We address this in the inverse optimal framework, thereby avoiding the need to solve the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equations, and establish a general result that is optimal with respect to a meaningful cost.

arxiv-2510-08151.title: Evaluating multi-season occupancy models with autocorrelation fitted to heterogeneous datasets
arxiv-2510-08151.creator: André Luís Luza, Didier Alard, Frédéric Barraquand
arxiv-2510-08151.description: Abstract Predicting species distributions using occupancy models accounting for imperfect detection is now commonplace in ecology. Recently, modelling spatial and temporal autocorrelation was proposed to alleviate the lack of replication in occupancy data, which often prevents model identifiability. However, how such models perform in highly heterogeneous datasets where missing or single-visit data dominates remains an open question.

arxiv-2601-05922.title: Abelian surfaces in Hesse form and explicit isogeny formulas
arxiv-2601-05922.creator: Thomas Decru , Sabrina Kunzweiler
arxiv-2601-05922.description: Abstract . We develop a new method for the computation of ( 3 , 3 ) (3,3) -isogenies between principally polarized abelian surfaces. The idea is to work with models in ℙ 8 \mathbb{P}^{8} induced by a symmetric level- 3 3 theta structure.

pmc-11353052.title: Household Income Is Associated with Chronic Pain and High-Impact Chronic Pain among Cancer Survivors: A Cross-Sectional Study Using NHIS Data
pmc-11353052.creator: Nimish Valvi, Javier A Tamargo, Dejana Braithwaite, Roger B Fillingim, Shama D Karanth, Yusuke Shiozawa
pmc-11353052.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryPain is a common symptom that affects individuals with cancer. This study, using data from the National Health Interview Survey, explored how household income relates to chronic pain among cancer survivors. It found that lower-income survivors, those below 200% of the federal poverty level (FPL), were more likely to report chronic pain lasting at least 3 months and pain that significantly limited their daily activities.

pmc-12649367.title: A Frequency-Dependent and Nonlinear, Time-Explicit Five-Layer Human Head Numerical Model for Realistic Estimation of Focused Acoustic Transmission Through the Human Skull for Noninvasive High-Intensity and High-Frequency Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation: An Application to Neurological and Psychia
pmc-12649367.creator: Shivam Sharma, Nuno A. T. C. Fernandes, Óscar Carvalho
pmc-12649367.description: Transcranial focused ultrasound is a promising noninvasive technique for neuromodulation in neurological and psychiatric disorders, but accurate prediction of acoustic transmission through the skull remains a major challenge. In this study, we present a five-layer numerical human head model that integrates frequency-dependent acoustic parameters with nonlinear time-explicit dynamics to realistically capture ultrasound propagation.

pmc-12670789.title: High physical activity is associated with decreased fungiform papillae area and number, elevated sucrose recognition thresholds, and increased IL-6 levels: an observational human study
pmc-12670789.creator: Isabella Kimmeswenger, Marlies Gaider, Kevin Doppelmayer, Jakob P Ley, Barbara Lieder
pmc-12670789.description: BackgroundDisease-related inflammation affects chemosensory signaling, but knowledge on the impact of exercise-induced low-grade inflammation on taste function remains scarce. Here we hypothesized that intense habitual physical activity modifies sweet taste perception via increased cytokine release.MethodsIn an observational human study we compared participants (m/f) engaging in high (n = 34) and low (n = 31) levels of habitual physical activity.

pmc-12732788.title: Transforming Wheat Straw into Superabsorbent Polymers for Sustainable Agricultural Management
pmc-12732788.creator: Andrey V Sorokin, Aidar I Kadyirov, Igor A Saranov, Egor M Tsimmer, Vladislav A Kiselev, Ivan A Zhuravlev, Maria S Lavlinskaya, Raffaella Aversa
pmc-12732788.description: The massive accumulation of agricultural waste, such as wheat straw, and its disposal by burning pose significant environmental challenges. This study explores a sustainable solution by converting wheat straw into composite superabsorbent polymers (SAPs)—superabsorbents contain both synthetic and biodegradable fragments—for improved agricultural water and nutrient management.

pmc-12928536.title: Advances in Eco‐Friendly Extraction of Fruit Bioactive Compounds: Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
pmc-12928536.creator: Abadi Gebreyesus Hndeya, Desta Berhe Sbhatu, Gebreselema Gebreyohannes
pmc-12928536.description: Fruit bioactive compounds such as polyphenols, carotenoids, vitamins and fibres provide important antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory and disease‐preventive benefits, but their extraction remains difficult due to poor solubility and the limitations of conventional methods that use toxic solvents, require high energy and often result in low yields.

pmc-12970029.title: A Brand-New Drainage Fluid Predictor, ICAM-1 for Implant Loss After the Immediate Reconstruction of Breast
pmc-12970029.creator: Chenyang He, Yezhen Jiang, Renyang Zhao, Jia Liu, Haiying Yang, Rongqiang Zhang, Yang Zhao
pmc-12970029.description: BackgroundNearly 40% of breast cancer patients are ineligible for breast-conserving surgery. Immediate implant-based breast reconstruction is a preferred option for these patients. The most severe complication of this procedure is implant loss. Currently, there are no cytokines available to predict implant failure.

pmc-13071639.title: SAR-Guided Scaffold Innovation of Selective V2R Antagonists: Therapeutic Frontiers in ADPKD
pmc-13071639.creator: Haofeng Shi, Yinlong Li, Steven H. Liang
pmc-13071639.description: The vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) is a class A G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) that plays a pivotal role in the regulation of renal water homeostasis and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) through sustained activation of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling.

pmc-13145521.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1858 OUTCOMES OF NURSING HOME RESIDENTS PRESENTING AS FAST POSITIVE TO MAJOR STROKE CENTRE
pmc-13145521.creator: Christiaan Strydom, Emma Murtagh, Rachel Walsh, Daniel Ryan
pmc-13145521.description: Background and aimsNursing home (NH) residents represent a frail population at high risk of stroke, yet they are underrepresented in acute stroke trials. The Face Arm Speech Time (FAST) tool is widely used to expedite stroke recognition and transfer to specialist centres, but its appropriateness and outcomes in NH residents remain unclear.

pmc-13157566.title: #KneeOsteotomy: Evaluation of the Quality and Educational Value of TikTok Videos
pmc-13157566.creator: Moses K.D. El Kayali, Luis V. Bürck, Stephen Fahy, Alan Getgood, Benjamin Bartek, Tobias Jung, Stephan Oehme
pmc-13157566.description: Background:TikTok videos on orthopaedic topics receive high engagement, but the quality of content on knee osteotomies is unclear.Purpose:To assess the quality, reliability, and educational value of TikTok videos on knee osteotomy.Study Design:Cross-sectional study.Methods:TikTok was searched for “knee osteotomy,”“high tibial osteotomy,” and “distal femoral osteotomy,” yielding 789 videos. A total of 191 met inclusion criteria.

pmc-13623735.title: Trypanosoma cruzi modulates its histone post-translational modifications under nutritional stress
pmc-13623735.creator: Rafael Fogaça de Almeida, Lyris Martins Franco de Godoy
pmc-13623735.description: IntroductionHistone post-translational modifications (hPTMs) constitute one of the main regulatory mechanisms of chromatin state in eukaryotes. The presence of different hPTMs has been described in Trypanosoma cruzi; however, their roles in parasite biology and adaptation to environmental changes remain poorly understood.

pmc-13665009.title: Cynaroside Attenuates Ethinylestradiol-Induced Cholestatic Liver Injury by Modulating the FXR/BSEP/CYP7A1/SHP Axis
pmc-13665009.creator: Amany M. Hamed, Doha M. Al-Nouri, Nadia S. Mahrous, Asmaa Sabry Bassit, Azza M. A. Abouelella, Asmaa Hassan, Gehad S. Mokhtar, Ghada M. Ahmad, Ahmed S. Osman, Ahmed R. H. Ahmed, Aya A. E. Mahgoob, Shymaa A. Thabet, Hany M. R. Abdel-Latif, Ghalia Shamlan, Haifeng Zhao, Ammar Al-Farga, Safaa S. Solima
pmc-13665009.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cholestatic liver diseases are characterized by disrupted bile acid homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammation, ultimately leading to progressive hepatic injury. Although ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) remains the standard pharmacological therapy, its therapeutic efficacy is limited in several cholestatic conditions. This study investigated the hepatoprotective effects of cynaroside (CYN), a naturally occurring flavonoid glycoside, against ethinylestradiol (EE)-induced cholestatic liver injury and explored its underlying molecular mechanisms.
